name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican fundraising dominance ($2.1M vs $31K, plus $1.3M outside support)
Open seat with no incumbent on ballot
model.rationale: The district's R+25 lean and the Republican candidate's overwhelming financial advantage leave no plausible path for the Democrat, who has raised only about $31,000. Markets price the Republican at 99%, consistent with a safe Republican rating.
model.watch: A surprise Democratic fundraising surge or a divisive Republican primary runoff could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
West Texas's 19th District is deeply Republican, with a partisan lean of roughly 25 points to the right. Representative Jodey Arrington is retiring, but the seat remains firmly in the Republican column. Tom Sell has raised over $2.1 million and benefits from more than $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised about $31,000 with minimal cash on hand.

Prediction markets give the Republican a 99% chance of holding the seat, and no expert raters list this race as competitive. With no polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Republican win of roughly 20 points.
